mainTopic: Suffering and atonement (יסורין של אהבה, stories of the sick, רב הונא's wine), and אבא בנימין's teachings about תפילה and the bed
overview: This amud begins by finishing a ברייתא: one who learns תורה, does גמילות חסדים, and buries his children has all his sins forgiven. רבי יוחנן asks for the source for burying children, and an elder answers in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי with a גזירה שוה on the word עון. רבי יוחנן then teaches that נגעים and children are not יסורין של אהבה. The גמרא defends the נגעים half with three alternative answers, and explains that the children half refers to someone who never had children at all. Next come stories of חכמים visiting the sick: each sick person says he wants 'neither the suffering nor its reward', and the visitor takes his hand and raises him up. In the story of רב הונא's wine turning to vinegar, the חכמים teach that suffering should lead a person to examine his deeds, and his loss is restored once he fixes his conduct. The amud ends with teachings of אבא בנימין about davening close to bedtime, placing the bed between צפון and דרום, and not walking out on a friend who is still davening. Its final question, the reward for waiting, is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Burying one's children brings forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא: one who buries his children has all his sins forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and one who buries his children has all his sins forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a teaching that started on the previous amud. It lists three things that wipe away sins: learning תורה, doing גמילות חסדים, and burying one's own children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ברייתא says that whoever does תורה and גמילות חסדים, and buries his children, is forgiven for all his sins. This amud begins with only the last item, burying children. That item is the one רבי יוחנן will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buries his children (whose children die in his lifetime)
They forgive him; he is pardoned

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the tail of a longer sentence from the previous עמוד. The full list is תורה, גמילות חסדים, and burying children. Without the first two items, the next step will not make sense.

phrases.english: and one who buries his children —
phrases.notes: Continuation of the ברייתא recited before רבי יוחנן, which began with תורה and גמילות חסדים.

phrases.english: they forgive him for all his sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקוֹבֵר אֶת בָּנָיו מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ עַל כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who learns תורה, does גמילות חסדים, and buries his children has all his sins forgiven.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks for the source for burying children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן shows a פסוק for forgiveness through תורה and גמילות חסדים, then asks where burying children comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: It makes sense for תורה and גמילות חסדים, because it is written, 'With kindness and truth, sin is atoned.' 'Kindness' means גמילות חסדים, as it says, 'One who pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, righteousness, and honor.' 'Truth' means תורה, as it says, 'Buy truth and do not sell it.' But where do we learn that one who buries his children is forgiven?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן agrees that two of the three items have a clear source in a פסוק. He then challenges the third item, burying children, by asking where its source is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'בחסד ואמת יכפר עון' says that kindness and truth bring atonement. Two other פסוקים identify חסד as גמילות חסדים and אמת as תורה. Nothing in that פסוק mentions burying children, so that part of the ברייתא needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces the part that is fine before the difficulty)
From where? (a request for a source)

steps.whyThisMatters: The pattern 'בשלמא X… אלא Y מנין' appears throughout ש״ס. The גמרא first grants what already has a source, then points to the one piece that does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
phrases.notes: Said to the תנא who recited the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Granted, Torah and acts of kindness [atone],
as it is written: 'With kindness and truth, sin is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6).
phrases.notes: This is the main פסוק. The next lines identify what חסד and אמת mean.

phrases.english: 'Kindness' — this is acts of kindness,
as it is said: 'One who pursues righteousness and kindness
phrases.notes: Here חסד appears alongside צדקה, so it means acts of kindness toward others.

phrases.english: will find life, righteousness, and honor' (Mishlei 21:21).
'Truth' — this is Torah,
as it is said: 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23).
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues 'wisdom, guidance and understanding,' which shows that אמת refers to תורה.

phrases.english: But 'one who buries his children' — from where [do we know this]?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא תּוֹרָה וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the source for two items of the ברייתא and challenges the third.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's inclusion of קובר את בניו as a cause of forgiveness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'בחסד ואמת יכפר עון' supports only תורה (אמת) and גמילות חסדים (חסד). It does not mention burying children, so that item seems to have no source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source showing that burying one's children atones for sin.

steps.title: An elder answers with a גזירה שוה on the word עון
steps.stepSummary: An elder, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, links 'עון' in משלי to 'עון אבות' in ירמיהו, which ties a father's sin to his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder taught him in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: It is learned from 'sin' and 'sin.' Here it is written, 'With kindness and truth, sin is atoned,' and there it is written, 'He repays the sin of the fathers into the bosom of their children.'
steps.whatsHappening: An old man answers רבי יוחנן's question. He uses a matching word, עון, to connect the atonement פסוק to a פסוק about children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו, the עון of the fathers is 'paid' into the bosom of the children, so the children's suffering pays off the father's sin. Through the shared word עון, this kind of payment is linked to 'יכפר עון.' The conclusion is that the death of one's children also brings atonement to the father.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder (an unnamed old man)
It comes / it is learned (introduces a derivation)
A derivation linking two פסוקים through a shared word (here, עון)
Here … there (the two פסוקים being compared)

steps.whatToRemember: Burying children atones because of the גזירה שוה עון–עון. The fathers' עון is 'paid' through the children, and that payment counts as atonement.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק in ירמיהו sounds like a punishment, not a kindness. The point is that this painful payment wipes the father's slate clean, which is why it counts as atonement.

phrases.english: A certain elder taught him,
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is learned from 'sin' and 'sin.'
phrases.notes: The same word, עון, appears in both פסוקים. This creates the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'With kindness and truth, sin is atoned,'
and it is written there: 'And He repays the sin of the fathers
into the bosom of their children' (Yirmiyahu 32:18).
phrases.notes: The father's sin is paid off through the children, and so the father receives atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתְיָא עָוֹן עָוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי יוחנן's question 'מנין.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the word עון links 'יכפר עון' to 'משלם עון אבות אל חיק בניהם,' showing that burying children atones for the father's sins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supplying a missing source through a גזירה שוה

steps.title: נגעים and children are not יסורין של אהבה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן states that נגעים and suffering through children are not counted as יסורין של אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Leprous afflictions and children are not afflictions of love.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the wider topic of suffering with a new statement from רבי יוחנן. He excludes two types of suffering from the category of 'suffering of love.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: יסורין של אהבה is suffering that השם sends out of love, not as punishment for a specific sin. רבי יוחנן says נגעים and suffering connected to children do not fall into that category. The גמרא will challenge each half: the נגעים half from a ברייתא that calls them a מזבח כפרה (step 5), and the children half from רבי יוחנן's own conduct with his tenth son's bone (step 9).

keyTerms.meaning: Afflictions of love: suffering sent out of love, not as punishment

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement sets up the next discussion. The גמרא tests both halves against other sources and ends up defining exactly which נגעים and which 'children' case רבי יוחנן meant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Leprous afflictions and children —
phrases.notes: 'Children' refers to suffering related to children. The גמרא will soon define which case is meant.

phrases.english: are not afflictions of love.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נְגָעִים וּבָנִים אֵינָן יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement by רבי יוחנן on suffering. It moves from atonement through suffering to the narrower category of יסורין של אהבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נגעים and suffering through children are excluded from the category of יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says נגעים bring atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with a ברייתא that calls the four types of נגעים a מזבח כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are נגעים really not suffering of love? But a ברייתא taught: anyone who has one of these four kinds of נגעים, they are nothing but an altar of atonement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 4. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to treat נגעים as a good, cleansing kind of suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said נגעים are not יסורין של אהבה. The ברייתא says נגעים are a מזבח כפרה, an altar that wipes away sin, which sounds like loving suffering. So the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Skin afflictions (צרעת) described in ויקרא פרק יג
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
Appearances or shades (the four types of נגעים)
An altar of atonement, meaning something that brings forgiveness

phrases.english: And are leprous afflictions not [suffering of love]?
phrases.notes: Refers back to רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 4.

phrases.english: But it was taught: anyone who has on him
phrases.notes: וְהָתַנְיָא signals a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: one of these four appearances of afflictions,
they are nothing but an altar of atonement!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְגָעִים לָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 4 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that נגעים are not יסורין של אהבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls נגעים a מזבח כפרה, which implies they are a positive, loving kind of suffering.

steps.title: Atonement is not the same as love
steps.stepSummary: נגעים do bring כפרה, but they are still not יסורין של אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are an altar of atonement, but they are not suffering of love.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both sources can be true at the same time. נגעים wipe away sin, but they are a different category from יסורין של אהבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that anything bringing כפרה must be יסורין של אהבה. The answer separates the two ideas. Suffering can cleanse a person of sin without being the special loving suffering sent to someone who has no sin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying נגעים are bad or useless. They do bring כפרה. They just don't fit the narrower label of יסורין של אהבה.

phrases.english: An altar of atonement, they are;
suffering of love, they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִזְבַּח כַּפָּרָה הָווּ, יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה לָא הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 5 by splitting כפרה from יסורין של אהבה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything that brings כפרה counts as יסורין של אהבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: נגעים bring כפרה but are not יסורין של אהבה, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Different rules for בבל and ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the ברייתא speaks about us in בבל, and רבי יוחנן speaks about them in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: this one is for us, and that one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to answer the challenge. Each source is talking about a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רש"י and רב האי גאון, people in ארץ ישראל were very strict about טומאה, so a מצורע was sent away from society and suffered greatly. In בבל they were less strict, so the suffering was lighter and could count as loving. So the ברייתא (loving suffering) fits בבל, and רבי יוחנן (not loving) fits ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another answer)
This one... and that one (assigns each source to a different case)
For them (the sages of ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
This one is for us, and that one is for them.
phrases.notes: Us = בבל, where the ברייתא applies. Them = ארץ ישראל, where רבי יוחנן's rule applies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא לָן וְהָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the challenge in Step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources describe the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא fits בבל, where a מצורע suffers less. רבי יוחנן fits ארץ ישראל, where a מצורע is sent away.

steps.title: Hidden נגעים versus visible נגעים
steps.stepSummary: Third answer: the ברייתא speaks about a hidden נגע, and רבי יוחנן speaks about a visible one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: this one is in private, and that one is in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third way to answer the challenge. The difference depends on where on the body the נגע appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נגע on a hidden part of the body does not embarrass the person or push others away, so it can be יסורין של אהבה, as the ברייתא says. A visible נגע causes people to keep their distance and brings shame, so רבי יוחנן says it is not יסורין של אהבה.

keyTerms.meaning: In private, on a hidden part of the body
In public, on a visible part of the body

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says נגעים are a מזבח כפרה, and רבי יוחנן says they are not יסורין של אהבה. The גמרא gives three ways to resolve this. (1) כפרה is not the same as love. (2) בבל differs from ארץ ישראל. (3) A hidden נגע differs from a visible one.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
This one is in private, that one is in public.
phrases.notes: Private = the ברייתא (can be loving). Public = רבי יוחנן (not loving).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא בְּצִנְעָא הָא בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, independent answer to the challenge in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by whether the נגע is visible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All נגעים are the same, so the two sources contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A hidden נגע can be יסורין של אהבה. A visible נגע, which brings shame and isolation, is not.

steps.title: How can losing children not be suffering of love?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'children' part of רבי יוחנן's statement. רבי יוחנן himself lost ten sons and treated that loss as meaningful suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And suffering through children is not יסורין של אהבה?! What case are we talking about? If you say someone had children and they died, didn't רבי יוחנן himself say, 'This is the bone of my tenth son'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the second half of רבי יוחנן's statement, the part about children. It asks what case he meant and shows that one possible case contradicts his own behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן lost ten children. He carried a bone of his tenth son and showed it to mourners to comfort them. That shows he saw the loss of children as suffering that comes from God's love, so how could he say suffering through children is not יסורין של אהבה?

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? (asks which exact case is meant)
If you say (introduces a possible case that will be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן did not show the bone to complain. He used it to comfort others: 'Look, I suffered too, and I accepted it.' That is exactly why it counts as יסורין של אהבה.

phrases.english: And children are not [suffering of love]?!
What are the circumstances?
If you say that he had them and they died
but didn't Rabbi Yochanan say
'This is the bone of my tenth son'?
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן used this bone to comfort mourners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָנִים לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the נגעים half of רבי יוחנן's statement in steps 5-8, the גמרא turns to the children half.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim (step 4) that suffering through children is not יסורין של אהבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's own conduct, showing his tenth son's bone to comfort others, shows that he treated the loss of children as יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: Never having children is different from losing them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's rule is about someone who never had children. Someone who had children who died can still be experiencing יסורין של אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this ruling (not suffering of love) is about someone who never had children at all. That case (suffering of love) is about someone who had children and they died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by splitting the children case into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having no children at all is not counted as יסורין של אהבה. Losing children who were born, like רבי יוחנן did, can be. So there is no contradiction between רבי יוחנן's statement and his own life.

keyTerms.meaning: This case… and that case (splits into two situations)

steps.whatToRemember: For נגעים, the גמרא offers three alternative explanations of רבי יוחנן (steps 6-8). For children, his rule refers only to someone who never had children, while losing children can be יסורין של אהבה (step 10).

phrases.english: Rather, this one
is where he had none at all
and that one
is where he had them and they died

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּלָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: two different situations under the heading of 'children'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's 'children' meant losing children, which contradicts his own experience.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן meant someone who never had children. Losing children can be יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן visits and heals רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבי חייא בר אבא is sick. רבי יוחנן asks whether he loves his suffering. He says he wants neither the suffering nor its reward, and רבי יוחנן takes his hand and raises him up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא became sick. רבי יוחנן came to visit him and asked, 'Are your sufferings dear to you?' He answered, 'Neither them nor their reward.' רבי יוחנן said, 'Give me your hand.' He gave him his hand, and רבי יוחנן raised him up (healed him).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from discussing rules about suffering to a real story about how חכמים dealt with suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Accepting suffering with love brings great reward. Still, רבי חייא בר אבא says honestly that he would rather skip both the pain and the reward. Because he does not want the suffering, רבי יוחנן heals him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even great חכמים did not have to want suffering. Asking to be healed is legitimate.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba fell ill.
Rabbi Yochanan went in to visit him
He said to him: Are sufferings dear to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: Neither them nor their reward.
He said to him: Give me your hand.
He gave him his hand, and he stood him up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא חֲלַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of suffering with a story about חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick person may honestly refuse suffering and its reward, and a חכם can heal him.

steps.title: רבי חנינא visits and heals רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A parallel story: this time רבי יוחנן is sick. רבי חנינא visits, has the same conversation with him, and heals him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן became sick. רבי חנינא came to visit him and asked, 'Are your sufferings dear to you?' He answered, 'Neither them nor their reward.' רבי חנינא said, 'Give me your hand.' He gave him his hand, and רבי חנינא raised him up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the same story again, but now the healer (רבי יוחנן) is the sick one. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is almost word-for-word the same as the first story. The only change is who is sick and who heals. That change is what makes the next question jump out.

keyTerms.meaning: A senior חכם who visited and healed רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan fell ill.
Rabbi Chanina went in to visit him.
He said to him: Are sufferings dear to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: Neither them nor their reward.
He said to him: Give me your hand.
He gave him his hand, and he stood him up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲלַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A mirror-image of step 11, with roles reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רבי יוחנן, the healer, needed someone else to heal him.

steps.title: Why couldn't רבי יוחנן heal himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed רבי חנינא. If he could heal his student, he should have been able to heal himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he need רבי חנינא? Let רבי יוחנן raise himself up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a puzzle created by the two stories. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 showed that רבי יוחנן had the power to heal. So it seems strange that in step 12 he had to wait for רבי חנינא. The גמרא wants to understand why.

phrases.english: Why?
Let Rabbi Yochanan stand himself up!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי, לוֹקִים רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares step 11 with step 12 and finds a puzzle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story in step 12, where רבי יוחנן needed רבי חנינא to heal him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 11 shows רבי יוחנן could heal others, so he should have been able to heal himself.

steps.title: A prisoner cannot free himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers why רבי יוחנן needed רבי חנינא: a person who is 'locked up' cannot release himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: A prisoner cannot free himself from prison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13 with a short, well-known saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick person is like a prisoner. A prisoner may be able to unlock other people's chains, but he cannot unlock his own. In the same way, רבי יוחנן could heal רבי חייא בר אבא, but when he was the sick one, he needed רבי חנינא to heal him.

keyTerms.meaning: They say. This introduces a well-known saying or answer.

steps.whatToRemember: Even a great healer cannot heal himself. Help has to come from someone else.

phrases.english: They say:
A prisoner does not free himself
from the prison.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אֵין חָבוּשׁ מַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Analogy / general principle: a person cannot release himself from his own bonds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי יוחנן could heal others, he should have been able to heal himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Healing power works on others, not on oneself. A prisoner needs someone outside the prison to free him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן visits the sick רבי אלעזר and lights up the dark room
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: רבי אלעזר is sick in a dark room. רבי יוחנן uncovers his arm, light shines, and he sees רבי אלעזר crying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר fell ill. רבי יוחנן went in to visit him and saw that he was lying in a dark room. רבי יוחנן uncovered his arm, and light shone out. He saw that רבי אלעזר was crying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a third sickness story and sets the scene. This step prepares the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was famous for his beauty, and here light shines from his arm. This detail is important later, because רבי אלעזר's crying turns out to be about that very beauty. The crying is mentioned here so that רבי יוחנן can ask about it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Went in to him, visited him

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar fell ill.
Rabbi Yochanan went in to visit him.

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָא דַּהֲוָה קָא גָּנֵי בְּבֵית אָפֵל.
phrases.english: He saw that he was lying in a dark room.
He uncovered his arm
and light shone out.
phrases.notes: Light radiated from רבי יוחנן's beautiful skin.

phrases.aramaic: חַזְיֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה קָא בָּכֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: He saw that Rabbi Elazar was crying.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חֲלַשׁ. עַל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a third parallel story about visiting the sick, after the question about healing oneself has been answered
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבי יוחנן visits the sick רבי אלעזר, light shines from his arm, and רבי אלעזר is crying.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן offers three comforts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks why רבי אלעזר is crying and guesses three reasons: too little תורה, poverty, or lost children. He answers each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Why are you crying? If it is because you did not learn much תורה, we learned: whether someone does a lot or a little, it is the same, as long as he directs his heart to Heaven. If it is because you lack livelihood, not every person merits two tables. If it is because of children, this is the bone of my tenth son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tries to comfort his student by guessing why he is crying and giving an answer for each possible reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each guess has its own comfort. תורה: the amount does not matter as much as the heart's intention. Poverty: very few people get both wealth and תורה. Children: רבי יוחנן himself lost ten sons, so this kind of suffering happens even to great people. The third comfort connects back to steps 9-10, where loss of children could still be יסורין של אהבה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does much and one who does little are equal
As long as he directs his heart toward Heaven
Two tables, meaning both wealth and תורה
The bone of my tenth son

steps.confusionAlert: The line 'אחד המרבה ואחד הממעיט' originally comes from a משנה about קרבנות, big or small offerings. רבי יוחנן applies the same idea to learning תורה. Also, the 'bone' was a real keepsake that רבי יוחנן carried from his tenth son who died.

phrases.english: He said to him: Why are you crying?
If it is because of Torah that you did not learn much —
we learned: one who does much and one who does little are equal,
as long as he directs his heart toward Heaven.
And if it is because of livelihood —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כׇּל אָדָם זוֹכֶה לִשְׁתֵּי שֻׁלְחָנוֹת.
phrases.english: not every person merits two tables.
And if it is because of children —
this is the bone of my tenth son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי קָא בָּכֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by responding to the crying seen in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lack of Torah, poverty, and loss of children are not reasons for despair. Intention matters more than amount, few people get both wealth and Torah, and even great people lose children.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר cries over beauty that will decay
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that he is crying because רבי יוחנן's beauty will one day rot in the earth. רבי יוחנן agrees, and they both cry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to him: I am crying over this beauty of yours that will wear away in the dust. רבי יוחנן said to him: Over this you are certainly right to cry. And they both cried.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers רבי יוחנן's question. He is not crying about any of the three guesses, but about human mortality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three guesses were about רבי אלעזר's own suffering. His real reason is about someone else: seeing רבי יוחנן's beauty made him think about death. רבי יוחנן accepts that this is a proper reason to cry, and they cry together.

keyTerms.meaning: That wears away (decays) in the dust

phrases.english: He said to him:
Over this beauty that will decay in the dust
I am crying.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַל דָּא וַדַּאי קָא בָּכֵית,
phrases.english: He said to him: Over this you are certainly right to cry,
and they both cried.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַאי שׁוּפְרָא דְּבָלֵי בְּעַפְרָא קָא בָּכֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'Why are you crying?' from step 16 and sets aside all three of רבי יוחנן's guesses
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is crying because רבי יוחנן's beauty will one day decay in the grave.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן raises רבי אלעזר from his sickbed
steps.stepSummary: Following the same pattern as the earlier stories, רבי יוחנן asks whether suffering is dear to him. רבי אלעזר says no, and רבי יוחנן takes his hand and heals him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, רבי יוחנן said to him: Is suffering dear to you? He said: Neither the suffering nor its reward. רבי יוחנן said: Give me your hand. He gave him his hand, and רבי יוחנן raised him up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the same conversation and the same healing as in steps 11 and 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third time the same pattern appears. The sick person does not want the suffering, even with its reward, and the healer raises him up. It also matches step 14: רבי יוחנן can heal his student even though he could not heal himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of all this
And he raised him up (healed him)

steps.whatToRemember: All three stories teach the same lesson: even great people do not want suffering, even with its reward, and a visitor can help lift the sick person up.

phrases.english: Meanwhile
he said to him: Is suffering dear to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: Neither the suffering nor its reward.
He said to him: Give me your hand,
he gave him his hand,
and he raised him up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּהָכִי וְהָכִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲבִיבִין עָלֶיךָ יִסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבי אלעזר story using the same dialogue pattern as steps 11-12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר does not want suffering or its reward, and רבי יוחנן heals him by raising him up by the hand.

steps.title: רב הונא's wine turns sour and the חכמים tell him to examine his deeds
steps.stepSummary: 400 barrels of רב הונא's wine turn to vinegar. רב יהודה (or רב אדא בר אהבה) and the חכמים visit and tell him to examine his actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: 400 barrels of רב הונא's wine went sour. רב יהודה, the brother of רב סלא חסידא, came to him with the חכמים (some say it was רב אדא בר אהבה with the חכמים). They said to him: 'Let the master look into his deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story about suffering. A great financial loss happens to רב הונא, and his colleagues advise him to look into his own behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier stories asked whether a person welcomes suffering. This story takes a different angle: when suffering comes, a person should check his deeds. The visitors politely hint that something in רב הונא's behavior may need fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: Turned sour (the wine turned into vinegar)
And some say (introduces a different version of who was there)
Let the master examine his deeds

phrases.english: On Rav Huna there turned sour
four hundred barrels of wine.
phrases.notes: A huge financial loss.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda came in to him,
the brother of Rav Sala the Pious, together with the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Adda bar Ahava with the Sages,
phrases.notes: Two traditions about who the visitor was.

phrases.english: and they said to him: Let the master examine his deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא תְּקִיפוּ לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה דַּנֵּי דְחַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story about suffering, following the stories of רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When suffering comes, a person should examine his deeds.

steps.title: רב הונא asks if they suspect him
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא pushes back: 'Am I suspect in your eyes?'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Am I suspected of wrongdoing in your eyes?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא objects to the advice. He is saying that he has done nothing wrong, so why should he search his deeds?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge. It assumes the loss might be random and not a punishment. It also sets up the חכמים's reply.

phrases.english: He said to them: And am I suspect in your eyes?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי חֲשִׁידְנָא בְּעֵינַיְיכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the advice to examine his deeds.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רב הונא must have done something wrong.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He sees no sin in his conduct, so the advice seems to accuse him without reason.

steps.title: The חכמים answer that God does not punish without justice
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply: Is הקדוש ברוך הוא suspected of judging without justice?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'Is הקדוש ברוך הוא suspected of punishing without justice?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רב הונא's objection with a sharp question of their own. If you are not suspect, then God would be, and that is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is simple: the loss happened. Either רב הונא did something wrong, or God punished without a reason. The second option cannot be true, so there must be something to fix.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whyThisMatters: This states a basic principle in this part of ברכות: suffering is not random, so it should lead a person to look into his deeds.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מִי חֲשִׁיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
phrases.english: They said to him: Is the Holy One, Blessed be He, suspect
of carrying out judgment without justice?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי חֲשִׁיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּעָבֵיד דִּינָא בְּלָא דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question (reductio): denying any fault would mean God judges unjustly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא thought the loss might come without any wrongdoing on his part.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since God does not punish without cause, there must be something to examine.

steps.title: רב הונא asks them to tell him what they heard
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks: if anyone has heard something bad about me, let him say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'If someone heard something about me, let him say it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא accepts their point and asks them to tell him what he might have done wrong. This line sets up the next step, where they reveal the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His attitude has changed. He moves from defending himself to asking for information. This shows that he is honestly willing to look for a fault.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter (here: a report about something improper)

phrases.english: He said to them: If there is anyone
who heard something about me, let him say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִיכָּא מַאן דִּשְׁמִיעַ עֲלַי מִלְּתָא לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the principle and asks what the specific fault is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What wrongdoing have people heard about רב הונא?

steps.title: The חכמים say he withholds the tenant's share of vine branches
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell him they heard he does not give his אריס his share of the vine branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'This is what we heard: that the master does not give the vine branches to his tenant farmer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים name the problem: רב הונא does not give his tenant farmer the share of cut vine branches that the tenant deserves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אריס works the field in exchange for a share of what it produces. The vine branches (שביש) are part of what he is owed. Holding them back means withholding money that belongs to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Vine branches or shoots cut from the vines

phrases.english: They said to him: This is what we heard,
that the master does not give the vine branches to his tenant farmer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי שְׁמִיעַ לָן דְּלָא יָהֵיב מָר שְׁבִישָׁא לַאֲרִיסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's request to hear what was said about him.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He withholds the vine branches owed to his אריס.

steps.title: רב הונא defends himself: the tenant steals everything
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the tenant steals all his produce anyway, so withholding the branches is only taking back what is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Does he leave me anything of it? He steals all of it!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his behavior. He says the tenant is a thief, so keeping the branches only makes up for what was stolen from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His claim is that this is not theft but self-collection: he is taking back his own loss. Technically there may be some basis for this. The next step shows why it is still not acceptable for someone on his level.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי קָא שָׁבֵיק לִי
phrases.english: He said to them: Does he leave me
anything of it?
He steals all of it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָא שָׁבֵיק לִי מִידֵּי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against the accusation in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justification: withholding the branches is repayment for theft.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Withholding the branches looks like theft from the tenant.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא claims he is only taking back what the tenant stole.

steps.title: The חכמים reject his defense with a folk saying
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים quote a saying: one who steals from a thief still gets a taste of theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'This is what people say: Steal from a thief, and you still taste theft.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רב הונא's defense. Even if the tenant is a thief, taking back his share this way still carries a taste of stealing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They do not deny that the tenant steals. They reject the method: taking things on your own without a proper process still looks and feels like theft. For a person on רב הונא's level, even this is held against him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk proverb)
And you taste the taste (of theft)

steps.confusionAlert: The saying does not mean רב הונא was a plain thief. It means that taking back from a thief on your own still has a 'flavor' of theft, which matters for a great person.

phrases.english: They said to him: This is what people say:
"Steal from a thief, and you taste the taste (of theft)."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי בָּתַר גַּנָּבָא גְּנוֹב וְטַעְמָא טְעֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's defense.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that self-repayment makes the act acceptable.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Taking back from a thief on your own still has the character of theft.

steps.title: רב הונא commits to pay and his loss is restored
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא promises to give the tenant his share. Then his loss is restored: either the vinegar became wine again, or vinegar rose to the price of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'I take it upon myself to give it to him.' Some say: the vinegar turned back and became wine. And some say: the price of vinegar went up, and it was sold for the price of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא accepts the rebuke and fixes his behavior. The story ends with his loss being restored, and the גמרא brings two versions of how it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves the חכמים' point: the loss came because of a fault, and once he fixed it, the loss went away. The two versions differ only in whether a clear miracle happened or a natural price change.
steps.whatToRemember: When suffering comes, a person should examine his deeds, even small faults such as 'stealing back from a thief.' Once רב הונא fixed his behavior, his loss was restored.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: קַבֵּילְנָא עָלַי דְּיָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: I take it upon myself to give it to him.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: הֲדַר חַלָּא וַהֲוָה חַמְרָא.
phrases.english: Some say: the vinegar turned back and became wine.
And some say: the price of vinegar rose,
and it was sold at the price of wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבֵּילְנָא עָלַי דְּיָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב הונא accepts the rebuke from the previous step and repents.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Examining and correcting one's deeds removes suffering. רב הונא's loss was restored once he committed to pay his tenant.

steps.title: אבא בנימין's two lifelong concerns
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא בנימין: all his life he took great care about two things, his תפילה being 'before my bed' and his bed lying between צפון and דרום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אבא בנימין says: All my days I took great pains about two things: that my prayer should be before my bed, and that my bed should be placed between north and south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, in which אבא בנימין names two practices he was always careful about. This is the base text that the next steps will explain one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two practices are stated briefly and need explanation. The first, 'before my bed', is unclear: is it about place or time? The second, the direction of the bed, will later be tied to promised rewards.

keyTerms.meaning: Took pains, worked hard at, was concerned about
Between north and south (the bed's direction)

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Binyamin says:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים הָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר כׇּל יָמַי —
phrases.english: About two things I took great pains all my days —
about my prayer, that it should be before my bed,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל מִטָּתִי שֶׁתְּהֵא נְתוּנָה בֵּין צָפוֹן לְדָרוֹם.
phrases.english: and about my bed, that it should be placed between north and south.
phrases.notes: Explained in Steps 31-32.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story of רב הונא's wine ended in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא בנימין was careful that his תפילה be 'before his bed' and that his bed lie between צפון and דרום.

steps.title: What does 'before my bed' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the first half of the ברייתא and asks what 'before my bed' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'About my prayer, that it should be before my bed': what does 'before my bed' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on the first practice and asks for its meaning. This question sets up the next step, which tests one possible reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לפני מטתי' can mean in front of the bed (place) or before going to bed (time). The גמרא needs to know which one אבא בנימין meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean?

phrases.english: "About my prayer, that it should be before my bed":
What does "before my bed" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״לִפְנֵי מִטָּתִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the first practice listed in Step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'לפני מטתי' refers to a physical place or something else.

steps.title: It can't mean literally in front of the bed
steps.stepSummary: If 'before my bed' meant standing in front of the bed, that would clash with the rule that nothing may separate a person davening from the wall, learned from חזקיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it literally means in front of my bed, didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב (and some say רבי יהושע בן לוי): From where do we know that one who prays should have nothing separating between him and the wall? As it says: 'And חזקיהו turned his face to the wall and prayed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the literal reading and immediately attacks it. A bed between the person and the wall would be a blocking object, which is not allowed during תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From חזקיהו turning to the wall, we learn that a person davening should face a wall with nothing in between. If אבא בנימין stood in front of his bed, the bed would block him from the wall. So the literal reading would describe improper behavior, and it is unlikely a great תנא worked hard at that.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading about to be rejected)
And some say (a different name for who said it)
חזקיהו המלך, who turned to the wall to pray

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the bed itself. The problem is that the bed would stand between the person and the wall during תפילה.

phrases.english: If you say "before my bed" literally,
but didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said,
and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
From where do we know regarding one who prays

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דָּבָר חוֹצֵץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הַקִּיר —
phrases.english: that nothing should separate between him and the wall —
as it says: "And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall
and prayed"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ל״ח:ב

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא ״לִפְנֵי מִטָּתִי״ מַמָּשׁ, וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the literal answer to the question in Step 28 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'לפני מטתי' as physically standing in front of the bed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a rule that nothing should separate between a person davening and the wall. A bed in front of him would be such a separation.

steps.title: Read it as 'close to my bed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading: not 'before my bed' but 'close to my bed', meaning close in time to going to sleep or getting up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say 'before my bed'. Rather, say 'close to my bed'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading the words so that they are about timing, not location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'סמוך למטתי' means his תפילה was close in time to his bed, so there is no blocking object. רבינו חננאל explains he davened ערבית right before going to sleep. רש״י explains he davened שחרית as soon as he got up, before doing anything else.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say... rather say (rereading a text)

steps.whatToRemember: 'לפני מטתי' is about timing, davening close to going to bed or getting up, not standing in front of the bed, because nothing should separate a person from the wall during תפילה.

phrases.english: Don't say "before my bed",
rather say "close to my bed".

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא, ״לִפְנֵי מִטָּתִי״, אֶלָּא אֵימָא ״סָמוּךְ לְמִטָּתִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 29 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording (לא תימא... אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Before my bed' meant standing in front of the bed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means 'close to my bed' in time, so nothing separates him from the wall.

steps.title: A bed between north and south brings sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second practice and backs it up with רבי יצחק's teaching: one who places his bed between צפון and דרום will have sons, learned from 'וצפונך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And about my bed, that it should be placed between north and south.' For רבי חמא son of רבי חנינא said that רבי יצחק said: Whoever places his bed between north and south will have male children, as it says: 'And Your treasure (וצפונך) fills their belly; they will be satisfied with sons.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of the ברייתא and explains why the practice is worthwhile. It brings a teaching that promises sons to someone who sets up his bed this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a wordplay: 'וּצְפוּנְךָ' (Your treasure) sounds like 'צָפוֹן' (north). The same פסוק then says 'they will be satisfied with sons'. So a bed facing north is linked to having sons.

keyTerms.meaning: And Your treasure (sounds like צפון, north)
They will be satisfied / have plenty

steps.confusionAlert: Read the name as רבי חמא, son of רבי חנינא (one person), quoting רבי יצחק.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְעַל מִטָּתִי שֶׁתְּהֵא נְתוּנָה בֵּין צָפוֹן לַדָּרוֹם״.
phrases.english: "And about my bed, that it should be placed between north and south."
phrases.notes: The גמרא re-quotes the second half of the ברייתא to explain it.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said,
Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן מִטָּתוֹ בֵּין צָפוֹן לְדָרוֹם
phrases.english: Whoever places his bed between north and south
will have male children,
as it says: "And Your treasure fills their belly;
they will be satisfied with sons."
phrases.notes: תהלים י״ז:י״ד

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the first practice explained, the גמרא moves to the second practice from Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who places his bed between צפון and דרום merits sons.

steps.title: His wife will also not miscarry
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a second reward: his wife will not miscarry. He learns it by linking 'תמלא בטנם' to the 'full' pregnancy of רבקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Also, his wife will not miscarry. It is written here: 'And Your treasure fills their belly', and it is written there: 'And her days to give birth were filled, and behold, twins were in her belly.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds to רבי יצחק's teaching. Besides having sons, the man's wife will carry her pregnancies to full term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the root 'מלא' (fill) together with 'בטן' (belly). By רבקה, 'filled' means her pregnancy reached its full term. So 'Your treasure fills their belly' also means a full, healthy pregnancy with no miscarriage.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (linking two פסוקים)
Twins (יעקב and עשו in רבקה's belly)

steps.whatToRemember: Placing the bed between צפון and דרום is praised with two rewards: sons (רבי יצחק) and no miscarriage (רב נחמן בר יצחק).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Also, his wife will not miscarry.
It is written here: "And Your treasure fills their belly,"
and it is written there: "And her days to give birth were filled,
and behold, there were twins in her belly."
phrases.notes: בראשית כ״ה:כ״ד

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reward drawn from the same פסוק used in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In addition to having sons, the wife of one who places his bed between צפון and דרום will not miscarry.

steps.title: Leaving your friend alone in the middle of davening
steps.stepSummary: אבא בנימין teaches that if two people came to daven and one finished first and walked out without waiting for the other, his own תפילה is thrown back in his face. He brings a פסוק from איוב as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: אבא בנימין says: two people came in to daven. One of them started davening first, did not wait for his friend, and walked out. His own תפילה is torn up and thrown back in his face, as the פסוק says: 'You who tear your soul in your anger, for your sake shall the earth be abandoned?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching from אבא בנימין about two people davening together. Someone who finishes first and walks out, leaving his friend alone, loses the value of his own תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is two people davening together (according to רש"י, in a בית כנסת outside the city). One started first, so he finished first and left while his friend was still davening. Left alone, the friend gets nervous and cannot concentrate, so the one who left is punished: his own תפילה is 'torn' and rejected. The source is the word 'טֹרֵף' (tear) in the פסוק, which matches 'טוֹרְפִין' (they tear) in the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who taught this ברייתא and the earlier practices about davening and the bed
They tear / throw back (his תפילה is rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not misread the case as one person cutting his own davening short. He finished his own תפילה properly. His sin is walking out and leaving his friend alone while the friend is still davening.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the idea that you should not leave someone davening alone, especially in a place where he would feel unsafe or lose his concentration.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Abba Binyamin says:
Two people who came in to pray,
phrases.notes: According to רש"י, into a בית כנסת outside the city, where being alone is frightening.

phrases.english: and one of them began praying first,
and he did not wait for his friend, and he left.
his prayer is torn up and thrown back in his face,
as it is stated: 'He tears his soul in his anger,'
phrases.notes: איוב 18:4. 'Soul' here stands for his תפילה, which is a person pouring out his soul.

phrases.english: 'For your sake shall the earth be abandoned?'
phrases.notes: Meaning: do you think that because you left, your friend will be abandoned? הקדוש ברוך הוא still hears him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא. אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of אבא בנימין's practices about davening near his bed and the direction of his bed, the גמרא brings a different teaching of his about davening with another person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who finishes davening and leaves his friend alone while the friend is still davening has his own תפילה rejected, learned from 'טֹרֵף נַפְשׁוֹ בְּאַפּוֹ'.

steps.title: He also causes the שכינה to leave ישראל
steps.stepSummary: אבא בנימין adds a worse result: the person who left causes the שכינה to depart from ישראל. He learns it from the end of the same פסוק, 'the צור will be moved from its place', and proves that צור means הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, he also causes the שכינה to leave ישראל, as the פסוק says: 'And the Rock will be moved from its place.' And 'Rock' means only הקדוש ברוך הוא, as the פסוק says: 'The Rock who gave birth to you, you forgot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds a second, bigger consequence: walking out on your friend drives the שכינה away from ישראל. Then it proves from another פסוק that the word 'צור' refers to השם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses the next words of the same פסוק in איוב: 'וְיֶעְתַּק צוּר מִמְּקֹמוֹ' (the Rock will be moved from its place). To read this as the שכינה leaving, the ברייתא needs to show that צור means השם, so it brings 'צוּר יְלָדְךָ תֶּשִׁי' from דברים, where צור clearly refers to השם.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also (adds a further point)
And it will be moved / uprooted
Rock, a name for הקדוש ברוך הוא

steps.whatToRemember: Leaving your friend alone while he is still davening has two results: your own תפילה is rejected, and the שכינה leaves ישראל. Both come from the same פסוק in איוב.

phrases.english: And not only that, but he causes
the Divine Presence to depart from Israel,
as it is stated: 'And the Rock will be moved from its place.'
phrases.notes: The end of the same פסוק in איוב 18:4.

phrases.english: And 'Rock' means nothing other than the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is stated: 'The Rock who bore you, you neglected.'
phrases.notes: דברים 32:18. Here צור clearly refers to השם.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁגּוֹרֵם לַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁתִּסְתַּלֵּק מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds a second consequence, drawn from the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who leaves his friend alone while the friend is davening causes the שכינה to depart from ישראל, learned from 'וְיֶעְתַּק צוּר מִמְּקֹמוֹ', since צור means הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: What is the reward for waiting?
steps.stepSummary: Now the opposite case comes up: if the person does wait for his friend, what reward does he get? This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he waited for him, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Having heard the punishment for leaving, we now ask about the reward for staying. The answer comes on the next amud (6a).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is such a big punishment for leaving, it makes sense that there is a matching reward for waiting. The question flips the case from failing to do the right thing to doing it, and opens the door to the reward.

phrases.english: And if he waited for him,
what is his reward?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הִמְתִּין לוֹ מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Flips the case from the previous two steps (punishment for leaving) to the opposite case (reward for waiting).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward does someone get if he waits for his friend to finish davening instead of leaving him alone?
